Catalytic activity and stability of $\mathbf{I r}/\mathbf{T i O_{x}}@\mathbf{T i}$ for acidic OER The OER performance of $\mathrm{Ir/TiO_{x}@Ti}$ catalysts with varying Ir loadings (wt%) was systematically evaluated in 0.1M $\mathrm{H C l O}_{4}$ using a threeelectrode ymig.i.AhowninFig.aand Supplementary Fig. 14, geometric activity (current normalized by electrode area)exhibits a volcano-shaped dependence on Ir content, peaking at 24 wt%$\mathrm{Ir/TiO_{x}@Ti}$ .This optimal sample demonstrates a mass activity of 192 A/glrat1.5VusvrilehydrogctrdeRHE,Fig.b),.4-fold higher than unsupported Ir nanoparticles (81A/gr). The activity trend correlates directly with Ir utilization efficiency (Fig.3b, inset: At $<24\mathrm{w t}\%$ , incomplete $\mathsf{T i O}_{\mathsf{x}}@\mathsf{T i}$ surface coverage limits active site exposure; at >24 wt%, Ir nanoparticle agglomeration shields internal particles, reducing accessible active sites.

To probe the structural stability under harsh acidic OER conditions, inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectroscopy (ICP.OES) was employed to quantify Ir dissolution during electrolysis. As shown in Fig. 3c,$\mathrm{Ir/TiO_{x}@Ti}$ iexhibits a rapid initial dissolution phase (0-2h) followed by stabilization210h, total dissolution:.16mg/L),whereas unsupported Ir NPs show continuous dissolution over 8h (total dissolution: 0.6lmg/L). This 3.8-fold reduction in Ir leaching highlights the $\mathsf{T i O}_{\mathsf{x}}@\mathsf{T i}$ i support's critical role in anchoring Ir NPs and suppressing corrosion. Long-term chronopotentiometric testing at 10 mA/cm2 further reveals durabillity.$\mathsf{I r}/\mathsf{T i O}_{\mathsf{x}}@\mathsf{T i}$ undergoes an initial 10-hour activation phase, likely due to surface reconstruction into another active phase, and subsequently maintains stable operation for over 1700 h without degradation (Fig. 3d and Supplementary Fig. 15).
